bins.name: Brown bin
bins.accepts: Food scraps, yard waste, food-soiled paper

bins.name: Trash
bins.accepts: Anything that can't be recycled or composted

plastic_bottle.why: NYC takes rigid plastic bottles and jugs whatever the number on the bottom.

plastic_container.why: Rigid food containers, tubs, caps and lids are accepted.

prep: Foam cups go in the trash instead
plastic_cup.why: Rigid plastic cups and bowls are accepted.

prep: Leave on the container or toss in loose
plastic_lid_cap.why: Rigid plastic caps and lids are accepted.

prep: Better: return clean bags and film to a large store's drop-off
Never bag your recycling in black bags
plastic_bag_film.why: Plastic bags and film should not go in household recycling. Stores of 10,000+ sq ft must take them back.

snack_wrapper.why: Soft plastics like candy and snack wrappers can't be recycled in NYC.

prep: Never in the blue or brown bin
foam.why: Foam products like Styrofoam and packing peanuts go in the trash.

plastic_utensil_straw.why: NYC lists plastic cutlery as recyclable rigid plastic.

prep: Staples and window envelopes are fine
paper.why: Newspapers, magazines, mail and office paper go in paper recycling.

prep: Food-soiled bags go in the brown bin
paper_bag.why: DSNY rules list paper bags with mixed paper.

prep: Bundle big pieces with twine, 18 inches or smaller
cardboard.why: Flattened cardboard goes with mixed paper.

prep: Greasy box? Put it in the brown bin
pizza_box.why: Lightly-soiled pizza boxes go with paper; greasy ones are compostable.

prep: Clean tissues can go in the trash
soiled_paper.why: NYC composting takes food-soiled paper along with food scraps.

paper_cup.why: NYC accepts empty, dry paper cups with mixed paper.

carton.why: Milk, juice and soup cartons go with metal, glass and plastic.

metal_can.why: All kinds of metal are accepted, including food and drink cans.

aluminum_foil.why: Aluminum foil and trays are accepted.

prep: Anything still full is special waste
aerosol_can.why: Empty aerosol cans are accepted with metal.

metal_lid_scrap.why: NYC accepts all kinds of metal, including lids and small metal items.

glass_bottle_jar.why: Glass bottles and jars are accepted.

prep: Broken glass: seal in a box marked 'broken glass' or double-bag it
drinking_glass_ceramic.why: Drinking glasses, mugs and dishes can't be recycled.

prep: Bag in a clear, paper or compostable bag, or put in loose
food_scraps.why: Composting is mandatory in NYC. All food scraps are accepted, including meat and bones.

prep: Paper lawn bags or clear bags
yard_waste.why: Leaf and yard waste must be kept out of the trash.

prep: Tape the ends or bag each battery
Rechargeable and lithium-ion: take back to a store that sells them
Single-use alkaline (AA, AAA, 9V) may go in the trash
battery.why: Rechargeable and lithium-ion batteries must never go in trash or recycling. They start fires in trucks and plants.

prep: Use a store or nonprofit drop-off, a SAFE event, or ecycleNYC
electronics.why: It is illegal to put electronics in the trash or recycling in New York.

prep: Donate or use a textile drop-off
textile.why: Clothing can be donated or taken to textile recyclers instead of the trash.

shoes.why: Shoes count as accessories in NYC's clothing reuse guidance.

cigarette_butt.why: Items that can't be recycled or composted go in the trash.

prep: Pill packs with a foil back go in the trash

rope_string.why: Tanglers like cords, hoses and string lights jam sorting machines.

squeezable_tube.why: Plastic tubes and pouches, like toothpaste tubes, can't be recycled.

mask_gloves.why: Face masks and disposable gloves go in the trash.
